methods.name: Step by step
methods.reason: Newton's second law with Hooke's law: the spring pulls back in proportion to the stretch.

steps.title: Set up the equation of motion
steps.text: Newton's second law. \(kx\) is the spring force (Hooke's law), pulling back towards the unstretched position. \(cx'\) is the damping force, proportional to speed.

steps.title: Solve the equation
steps.text: The equation is linear with constant coefficients. Its characteristic equation gives the free motion: oscillation inside a decaying envelope when \(\zeta < 1\), the fastest return without overshoot when \(\zeta = 1\), and a slow return when \(\zeta > 1\). The constants are fixed by the starting displacement and velocity.

steps.title: List the known values
steps.text: Everything is converted to SI units before it goes into the equations.

steps.title: Find the natural angular frequency
steps.text: One period is the time for a full cycle. With \(T = 1.5\ \mathrm{s}\).

steps.title: Find the spring constant
steps.text: The natural angular frequency of a mass on a spring. With \(\omega_0 = 4.189\ \mathrm{rad/s}\), \(m = 2\ \mathrm{kg}\).

steps.title: Find the natural frequency
steps.text: Frequency is cycles per second. With \(T = 1.5\ \mathrm{s}\).

steps.title: Find the starting energy
steps.text: The starting energy is spring energy plus kinetic energy. With \(k = 35.09\ \mathrm{N/m}\), \(x_0 = 0.1\ \mathrm{m}\), \(m = 2\ \mathrm{kg}\), \(v_0 = 0\ \mathrm{m/s}\).

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Every found value was substituted back into the relations it appears in; they all hold.
